questions.question: Describe two environmental impacts of mining metals and explain how recycling metals reduces the impact.
questions.expected_answer: Mining removes vegetation and soil and creates waste rock and tailings dumps, destroying habitats and causing dust; acid mine drainage forms when sulphur compounds in exposed rock react with air and water, producing acid that dissolves heavy metals into rivers and groundwater; smelting ores uses coal and releases carbon dioxide and sulphur dioxide. Recycling metals means less ore must be mined, uses much less energy (recycled aluminium about 5 per cent of the energy) and keeps metal out of landfills.

questions.question: Explain why plastics cause long-lasting environmental problems and suggest three ways to reduce the problem.
questions.expected_answer: Plastics are made from fossil fuels and most do not biodegrade, so they persist for hundreds of years, breaking into microplastics that spread through oceans, soil and food chains; litter harms wildlife (turtles, seabirds, entanglement), blocks drains and pollutes beaches; burning plastic releases toxic smoke. Reduce single-use plastics (straws, bags); reuse durable bottles and bags; recycle plastics such as PET (1) and HDPE (2); support waste pickers and separate recyclables at home.

questions.question: Explain how burning coal for electricity affects the air, people's health and the climate, and suggest two ways to reduce these effects.
questions.expected_answer: Burning coal releases sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides and fine soot that pollute the air, especially on the Mpumalanga Highveld, causing asthma, lung disease and early deaths, and contributes to acid rain. It releases carbon dioxide, which traps heat and causes climate change, with more droughts, floods and rising seas. Reduce by using electricity efficiently (efficient bulbs, insulation, switching off) and by generating electricity from renewable sources such as solar and wind; also cleaner household energy instead of indoor coal or paraffin.
